text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament approved this year's programme for its participation in NATO's Partnership for Peace project. @

- Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi sharply criticised Slovakia yesterday for violating the Hungarian-Slovak basic treaty and related international agreements by banning bilingual school reports.

- Tamas Deutsch, commission chairman, announced that the Tocsik commission will summon Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Free Democrat president Ivan Peto to answer questions regarding the Tocsik affair next week. Socialist Party treasurer Laszlo Boldvai told the commission that its chairman aims to bring down himself and the Socialist Party rather than reveal the truth. @
- Transport Minister Karoly Lotz yesterday removed Sandor Kalnoki Kis from his post as president of the Hungarian state railway company MAV at Kalnoki's request.

- A road blockade planned for Friday by grape growers in south and east Hungary has split both the opposition and the Socialist Party amongst themselves in Parliament on whether to support or condemn the action.
- Consumer prices went up by 3.7 percent last month and by 18.9 percent in the previous 12 months, the Central Statistics Office reports. @
- Richter Gedeon, the country's second largest pharmaceutical firm, yesterday announced a 1996 profit of 11.35 billion forints on revenues of 36.8 billion forints.
- A three-day exhibition on state-of-the art bank technology opened yesterday in Budapest Sports Hall.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The December deficit of the balance of payments skyrocketed to $503 million. @
- The Health Insurance Authority and the National Health Insurance Fund have been ignoring laws and their own internal regulations since their formation, said a parliamentary commission.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will pay an official visit to Norway on February 18-19.
- Hungary will refuse to accept German pork, with immediate effect, in keeping with the European Commission's Tuesday decision to tighten its ban on such exports due to an outbreak of swine fever. @
NEPSZABADSAG
- Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha announced the names of state-owned companies whose shares will be exchanged for compensation coupons this year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- After raising 600 million to one billion forints through public share issue next month, shares of curtain manufacturer Gardenia will probably be listed on the stock exchange, reports this paper. @
- Inter-Europa Bank and the General Banking & Trust Co. may make bids for Polgari Bank when it is offered for sale. Daewoo and Hanwha are already known to be interested.
NEPSZAVA

- The investment bank Nomura has issued a "sell" recommendation to holders of Pannonplast shares, arguing that the company's earnings per share is likely to fall this year due to rising raw material prices.
